skill.name: email-notify
skill.description: Send SMTP email notifications when Codex or Claude tasks finish, using user-provided SMTP settings and task status details.
skill.summary: Send completion emails for Codex or Claude tasks through a configured SMTP server.
skill.author: caopulan

security_audit.summary: The skill legitimately sends SMTP messages and reads environment variables for SMTP configuration, including credentials. Most SKILL.md shell/backtick detections are Markdown or setup examples, but storing SMTP credentials in shell startup files is a real concern. No prompt injection text or unauthorized exfiltration intent was found beyond the configured email notification behavior.

remediation.issue: Plaintext SMTP credential guidance in shell startup files
remediation.suggestion: Recommend provider app passwords, a secret manager, or per-session environment injection instead of storing CODEX_EMAIL_PASSWORD in ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc.

remediation.issue: Email summaries may contain sensitive data
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger guidance to redact secrets, tokens, customer data, and private project details before sending notifications.

remediation.issue: SMTP recipients and sender are trusted from environment variables
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should restrict recipients and use a dedicated notification mailbox with least privilege.

remediation.issue: The workflow runs a Python helper from a shell command
remediation.suggestion: Keep command arguments quoted, avoid untrusted multiline content, and document dry-run verification before first use.

content.value_statement: Long AI tasks can finish when users are away from their editor. This skill sends SMTP email notifications with task status, project name, and a short summary.
actual_capabilities: Sends completion notifications through an SMTP or SMTPS server.
Reads SMTP host, port, sender, recipients, credentials, and TLS settings from environment variables.
Builds message content with device name, project name, status, and summary.
Can resolve a project name from AGENTS.md or the current folder.
Supports a dry-run mode that prints planned email fields without sending.
Validates required settings before attempting delivery.
limitations: Requires users to provide SMTP settings before use.
Does not manage OAuth or provider-specific app passwords.
Does not encrypt stored environment variables or shell profile entries.
Can expose sensitive summaries if users include secrets.

use_cases.title: Notify After Long Coding Runs
use_cases.description: Receive an email when a long Codex or Claude task finishes, including status and a short result summary.

use_cases.title: Track Team Automation Status
use_cases.description: Get completion alerts for shared project tasks without watching the terminal continuously.

use_cases.title: Monitor Maintenance Jobs
use_cases.description: Send a concise notification after scripted maintenance, test, or migration work completes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Completion Alert
prompt_templates.prompt: Notify me with email-notify when this task is complete. Use a short title, the final status, and a summary under 80 words.

prompt_templates.title: Project Status Email
prompt_templates.scenario: Include project context in the notification
prompt_templates.prompt: When you finish the refactor, send an email notification with the project name, final status, and concise summary.

prompt_templates.title: Failure-Only Notification
prompt_templates.prompt: After running tests, use email-notify only if the task is blocked or failed. Include the failing area and next action.

prompt_templates.title: Sanitized Migration Report
prompt_templates.prompt: At the end of this migration, send a sanitized email summary with status, completed steps, remaining risks, and no secrets.

output_examples.input: Notify me after the test run finishes.
output_examples.output: Email sent with subject "Test run complete" and a short body showing device, project, status, and summary.

output_examples.input: Send a blocked notification for the deployment review.
output_examples.output: The notification reports blocked status, names the project, and explains the missing approval.

output_examples.input: Use a dry run before sending the first notification.
output_examples.output: The dry run displays the planned SMTP host, sender, recipients, subject, and body without sending mail.

best_practices: Use provider app passwords and restrict the SMTP account to notifications.
Keep summaries short and remove secrets, tokens, and customer data.
Use dry-run first to verify host, sender, recipients, and message content.
anti_patterns: Putting API keys, passwords, or private data in the summary.
Configuring broad recipient lists for sensitive projects.
Leaving SMTP credentials in shared shell profiles or dotfiles.

faq.question: What does this skill send?
faq.answer: It sends an email with device name, project name, task status, and a short summary.

faq.question: Does it require an SMTP account?
faq.answer: Yes. Users must provide SMTP host, port, sender, recipients, and any required credentials.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is documented for Codex, Claude, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it send emails automatically?
faq.answer: It sends when the workflow runs the helper script with task title, status, and summary values.

faq.question: Can I preview the notification?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper supports dry-run mode to show planned fields without sending mail.

faq.question: What should I avoid in summaries?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, tokens, credentials, customer data, and private project details that should not leave the workspace.
